analysis.title: UBS House View Briefcases - Top 10 questions answered
key_insights: UBS CIO expects 25-basis-point Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 and does not think a measured tightening cycle will derail the US economy or the equity rally. The FOMC held rates in October after a 25 bp hike in September.
September US CPI was above consensus, with core CPI at 2.6% y/y. The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.36% in early October, the highest intraday level since 2002, and has since eased to about 4.95%.

UBS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027, and expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 25-30%. It recommends staying invested in diversified equities and reducing concentrated single-stock positions.

Preferred US sectors are consumer discretionary, financials, health care, industrials and utilities. UBS is positive on Eurozone equities (banks, consumer discretionary, health care, industrials, IT, Germany) and expects 15% European EPS growth in both 2026 and 2027.

UBS forecasts aggregate AI capex of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. Risks are rising in the more capital-intensive parts of the AI buildout, where funding pressure and execution risk could reinforce each other.

Cloud growth is accelerating: Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y (82% prior quarter, 34% in the March quarter), Azure +48% (43% in June quarter), Oracle cloud +62% (from 47%). Amazon's cloud unit accelerated for a sixth straight quarter.
AI-linked stocks sold off on 30 October, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 7.2% on new scrutiny of AI spending into earnings season.

UBS rates fixed income Attractive. It favors medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds and medium-maturity credit from stronger investment grade issuers, and is cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit. It also likes EM credit and high yield, with EM sovereign yields near 7.1% and corporate yields near 7%.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to a seven-week low of 4.93% on 30 October. The 10-year and 2-year yields were 4.91% and 4.58% in the week's summary, lowest since mid-September.

France's 10-year yield rose 6 bp to 4.97% after reaching above 5.14% the prior week, the highest since 2002. The spread to Bunds was 165 bp after a 177 bp peak, the widest since 2011. France's Q3 GDP contracted 0.1%.

Fitch affirmed France at A+ on 30 October but moved the outlook to negative. Moody's holds Aa3 with a negative outlook. UBS sees gradual deterioration, not an imminent funding crisis, and expects European borrowing costs to fall into next year.

Brent fell about 4.5% on 2 November to below USD 110 on Iran-Qatar talks, after ending October at a six-month high and touching USD 118/bbl on Friday. No agreement has been announced, and Hormuz flows and shipping security remain fragile.

Middle East-to-Asia crude shipping costs USD 30-40 a barrel versus under USD 5 before the conflict. Global refinery throughput was 81.8 million barrels a day in September, 2.8 million below a year earlier.
Dutch TTF gas hit a record EUR 104/MWh on 30 October. UBS favors broad, actively managed commodity exposure, citing copper demand from AI and electrification and El Niño risk to agriculture.

Spot gold fell to USD 3,875 an ounce, below USD 4,000, down 7% in October (second monthly decline) and about 17% below the August peak. UBS stays constructive, expects central bank buying of 750-1,000 tonnes a year, and calls dips below USD 4,000 a buying opportunity. It suggests a mid-single-digit allocation.

UBS advises holding cash for two to five years of net expected withdrawals and phasing excess cash into markets. US stocks beat cash in 97% of 10-year and 100% of 20-year periods between 1945 and July 2026. The S&P 500 has tended to rise about 10% in the 12 months after the first hike of a cycle.

In alternatives, UBS favors discretionary macro and low-net/market-neutral equity hedge funds, and sees private equity's discount to public equities near all-time highs. Preqin forecasts private markets AUM above USD 34trn by 2031.

Innovation themes are AI, Power and resources (annual power and grid investment of USD 3tr by 2030) and Longevity. UBS forecasts 12% annual GLP-1 revenue growth through 2030 and global longevity market revenue of USD 8tr by 2030.

trade_ideas.description: Add medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds as yields offer income and price-gain potential
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS believes market pricing of central bank tightening is too aggressive.
trade_ideas.risk: Fiscal sustainability concerns, AI-related debt issuance and elevated term premiums, especially at the longest maturities.

trade_ideas.description: Build or maintain a mid-single-digit gold allocation, using pullbacks below USD 4,000/oz as an entry
trade_ideas.rationale: Central bank buying, reserve diversification and elevated government debt support gold despite near-term pressure from real yields and a firm dollar.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated real yields and a firm US dollar.

trade_ideas.description: Hold broad, actively managed commodity exposure across energy, precious metals, industrial metals and agriculture
trade_ideas.rationale: Diversification and protection against prolonged energy disruption and inflation.
trade_ideas.risk: Price swings and futures or physical holding costs.

trade_ideas.description: Use rallies to move concentrated megacap tech positions into structured strategies with capital preservation

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening and elevated long-term yields.
Fiscal sustainability concerns, rising hyperscaler debt issuance and elevated term premiums.
Funding pressure and execution risk in capital-intensive parts of the AI buildout, and concentrated market performance.
Renewed escalation in the Middle East, especially attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure, and shipping and insurance costs.
French fiscal trajectory, with further spread widening possible.
Near-term gold pressure from higher real yields and a firm US dollar.
Alternatives carry illiquidity, strategy complexity and lockup risks.
vol_and_positioning: Equity-market risk aversion last week lifted high-quality bonds and lowered Treasury yields. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 7.2% on 30 October.
Commodities showed a correlation of 0.44 with global equities and -0.04 with US bonds from January 1999 through May 2026.
UBS suggests investors with concentrated megacap tech positions use rallies to rebalance into structured strategies with some capital preservation.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: Iranian and Qatari officials held a third day of talks on 2 November. No agreement has been announced.
Strait of Hormuz: Middle East crude flows have moved closer to pre-conflict levels but remain volatile. The strait carried about one-fifth of world oil and LNG before the conflict.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have escalated in recent weeks, and attacks on regional energy infrastructure and shipping continue.
France: political fragmentation and planned protests complicate fiscal consolidation.
Fitch revised France's outlook to negative on 30 October.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects strong earnings growth (25% in 2026, 14% in 2027) and GDP near 3% to let equities absorb two 25 bp hikes. Past downturns generally began at least two years after hikes started.
tension_points.bear_case: Strong data and high energy prices raised inflation concerns and pushed the 10-year yield to 5.36%. Valuation and AI funding risks rise with higher yields.

tension_points.bull_case: Iran-Qatar talks progressing, Brent down about 4.5% to below USD 110 and Saudi exports recovering.
tension_points.bear_case: No agreement announced, Hormuz flows volatile, attacks on infrastructure and shipping continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed escalation, particularly attacks spreading from military to civilian and energy infrastructure.
